processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental steel Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si (mass fraction) was melted in a vacuum induction furnace.
After melting the ingot was hot forged.
Specimens were heated to 1200 °C and held for 60 min prior to hot rolling.

processing_steps.method: six-pass hot rolling on a φ350 mm × 350 mm high-stiffness two-high hot rolling mill
processing_steps.temperature: initial rolling temperature 1100 °C, final rolling temperature 880 °C
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Six-pass rolling; initial rolling temperature 1100 °C, final rolling temperature 880 °C.

processing_steps.method: cold rolling on a four-high reversible cold rolling mill
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cold rolling experiment with a total reduction ratio of 60 % performed on the hot-rolled specimens.
The cold-rolled specimen was annealed at 850 °C for 30 min, then air-cooled to room temperature; this distinguishes ANT850 from ANT750/ANT800.
After annealing and air cooling, specimens were held at 400 °C for 30 min and air-cooled, yielding ANT850.

structures.overall_structure: Ferrite + bainite dual-phase (bainitic) structure with <5 % retained austenite; the 850 °C annealed condition is predominantly smooth dark ferrite matrix with only sparse bright bainitic network remnants.

phases_present.morphology: dark, flat, smooth regions (matrix); predominantly smooth dark matrix for the 850 °C condition
bright, rough-etched network (sparse remnants in AN850)

interfaces.phase_evolution: Ferrite volume fraction increases to 69 % and bainite decreases to 30.8 % at 850 °C compared with the 750/800 °C conditions; retained austenite content remains <5 % and its strengthening contribution is neglected.
interfaces.interface_notes: No explicit phase-interface structure or defect-interaction data specific to ANT850 is reported in the text.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests performed on an Instron 3382 universal electronic materials testing machine; three samples were tested for each group; air-cooled condition.

ultimate_tensile_strength.value: close to 1300 MPa (between the 1200 and 1400 MPa gridlines)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of the 850 °C (blue) specimen, Fig. 12

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Absolute difference between predicted and measured YS at 850 °C: plain Extra Trees = 36 MPa (predicted 928 MPa), GA-Extra Trees = 19 MPa (predicted 945 MPa), i.e. the difference was reduced by 17 MPa by GA optimisation

characterization_methods.technique: Secondary-electron SEM imaging, with ferrite/bainite grain size and volume fraction statistics using Image-Pro Plus software
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ETD detector, 20.00 kV, spot 5.9, mode Custom, magnification 3,000×, WD 10.7 mm, 40 µm scale bar (Fig. 13c for AN850)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Secondary-electron imaging of polished/etched specimens; several SEM images statistically analysed per group and average values calculated
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine ferrite and bainite volume fractions and average grain sizes for the AN850 specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN850: ferrite volume fraction 69 % (average grain size 6.8 μm), bainite volume fraction 30.8 % (average grain size 2.6 μm); predominantly smooth dark ferrite matrix with sparse bright bainitic network.

characterization_methods.technique: EBSD (Kernel Average Misorientation, KAM) analysis to obtain GND density via ρGND = 2θ/(μb) and Taylor factor statistics
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD scanning step size 0.2 μm (Fig. 14c and 14f for AN850)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EBSD scanning with 0.2 μm step size; KAM-based GND density and Taylor factor distribution
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify geometrically necessary dislocation density and Taylor factor for dislocation-strengthening calculation
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN850: GND density 0.72×10^14 m^-2 and average Taylor factor 3.53.

characterization_methods.technique: Room-temperature uniaxial tensile test (engineering stress-strain curve)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Instron 3382 universal electronic materials testing machine
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, strain rate 5×10^-4 s^-1, gauge 15 mm × 5.0 mm × 1.0 mm; three samples per group
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the yield strength and engineering stress-strain behaviour of the annealed specimens to validate the YS prediction framework
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN850 measured yield strength 964 MPa; the 850 °C curve shows the steepest rise to the highest peak (close to 1300 MPa) then softens and terminates just below 10 % strain.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical strengthening-mechanism calculation (solid solution, grain refinement, dislocation strengthening) combined into σ_YS = σ0 + σg + σd + σOrowan (linear superposition model)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Inputs: chemical composition Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si (mass fraction); ferrite/bainite volume fractions and grain sizes; GND density 0.72×10^14 m^-2; Taylor factor 3.53 for AN850
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Theoretical σy for AN850 = 926 MPa versus measured actual value 964 MPa (model overestimates by 38 MPa).

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute σ0 (matrix/friction + solid solution contribution) via eq. (6)
analytical_models.model_note: Where [x] is the mass percentage of elements; friction stress of the matrix is included in the solid solution strengthening.

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute σg via Hall-Petch (eq. 7) with mixing rule (eq. 8)
analytical_models.model_note: σg = K d^-1/2 and σg = fα σα + fβ σβ, with fα, fβ the ferrite and bainite volume fractions.

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute σd via Taylor hardening (eq. 9) with GND density from KAM (eq. 10)
analytical_models.model_note: σd = αMGbΔρ^1/2; ρGND = 2θ/(μb) with μ the EBSD step size (0.2 μm); GND contribution during elastic deformation is small compared with statistically stored dislocations.

computational_details.simulation_method: Machine-learning yield-strength prediction using GA-optimised Extra Trees (GA-Extra Trees) regression; comparison with plain Extra Trees
computational_details.software_used: Python framework; DEAP 1.3.3 for genetic-algorithm hyper-parameter search
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: GMM-augmented dataset of 776 samples (from 177 original literature entries)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Input features: contributions of solid solution, grain refinement, dislocation and Orowan strengthening; output: YS; dataset split 7:3 train/test; GA population size 30, crossover 0.7, mutation 0.3, 30 generations (convergence after 26th generation); optimised hyper-parameters n_estimators=1657, max_depth=51, min_samples_split=3, min_samples_leaf=1.0, max_features=0.85, max_samples=0.92
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: For the 850 °C (ANT850) case: Extra Trees predicted 928 MPa (difference 36 MPa) and GA-Extra Trees predicted 945 MPa (difference 19 MPa) against the measured 964 MPa; average error of the experimental validation across 750-850 °C was 1.56 %.

unmapped_findings: For ANT850 (AN850) the theoretical superimposed yield strength is σy = 926 MPa versus a measured actual value of 964 MPa (difference of 38 MPa), based on σ0 = 220 MPa, σg = 292 MPa, σd = 414 MPa and σOrowan = 0 MPa (Table 3).

The Orowan strengthening contribution for this steel is 0 MPa because the Al and Si additions suppress carbide formation, so no significant precipitation strengthening occurs; retained austenite content is <5 % and its strengthening contribution is neglected.
GA optimisation of the Extra Trees model reduced the YS prediction difference at 850 °C by 17 MPa (from 36 MPa for plain Extra Trees to 19 MPa for GA-Extra Trees).
ANT850 GND density is 0.72×10^14 m^-2 and the average Taylor factor is 3.53 (Fig. 14c and 14f), which underlie the dislocation-strengthening contribution of 414 MPa.
The GA-Extra Trees model showed an average prediction error of 1.56 % across the experimental validation set of the Fe-3Mn-2Al-0.25C-0.4Si alloy annealed at 750-850 °C.

Fig. 13(c) is captioned 'AN800' but the citing text discusses AN750/AN800/AN850, so this micrograph (predominantly smooth dark ferrite matrix with sparse bright bainitic network) corresponds to the AN850 specimen (likely typographical error in the caption).
